Performance: the one-year strip, null = no price history. Checks: the summary wheel's traceable rules (always present; an axis that does not apply is absent). UserTarget: null = none set. NotableMoves: days whose return reached the threshold, each with the news and signals near it (#1218); null = no price history. Scorecard: the four-axis scorecard and its verdict word (spec 726 US2), null = it could not be read.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.API.Responses.LedgerScoreboardDto
member.summary: The Ledger scoreboard, "an arena of one" (#986, rallies comparison option B1): contestants graded over the same windows against the S&P 500, which is the zero line - every figure is excess return over it in percentage points, from the decision (or pick) to later. A decided proposal is one observation however its window overlaps another's, so the sample counts decisions, not days. Expired and superseded proposals are listed in and never scored.
member.param: The zero line's name: "S&P 500".
The ticker it is priced through: "SPY" (a price return, like the name's).
The scoring window after each decision or pick.
Scored rows a contestant needs before its figures can tell skill from luck.

LedgerAsProposed (every decided proposal as if followed and executed, signed by its direction), OwnerAsDecided (the owner's decision value, the one the Decisions page shows), then one PaperPicks row per candidate source (User, Ledger, Scan).

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Application.Commands.DecideThesisRevisionCommand
member.summary: The owner's verdict on a pending proposal. Confirm is the single step that writes: a promotion goes through (so the risk gate runs first and an override is the owner's alone), a narrative or trigger change through , a close through , each stamped as the owner's own write with the proposal's rationale and evidence in the audit. Reject needs the real reason, kept as the counterfactual. A decision claims the proposal first with one conditional Pending-to-decided write, so two overlapping decisions cannot both act; a confirm that writes nothing (risk gate refusal, a failure) releases the claim. Only the owner's own session decides: the handler refuses every other actor (a service token, the in-app agent, a job), so the boundary does not rest on a transport attribute alone.

member.summary: Deleting a thesis retires any news source registered to it (thesis-source staleness, orphaned half) before the delete runs: news_sources.ThesisId is ON DELETE SET NULL, so once the thesis row is gone the FK itself erases the only link back to it — this has to happen first, or a source silently reverts to looking like an ordinary market-wide default source with no record of why it stopped meaning anything. member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Application.Commands.PromoteCandidateCommand
member.summary: Promotes an Active candidate into a monitored (US3/FR-011). The 022 risk gate always runs first (FR-011b): a Refused verdict aborts with the named rule unless the caller passes , in which case the override is recorded as a signal (never silent — FR-007). Overriding is the owner's call alone: is ignored when is , so a Ledger promotion the gate refused stays refused (no thesis, no override signal) and the result says the override is owner-only. Invalidation triggers are the caller's when supplied, else the deterministic derived from the candidate's latest scorecard. Evidence at entry: the latest scorecard summary and the are carried into the thesis text and key data points. No scorecard degrades to an empty carry (the default text, no data points) and never fails the promotion. (a confirmed thesis-revision proposal) replaces those defaults field by field: whatever it leaves null keeps the scorecard-built text, data points and trigger prefill. (finance-sentry#704) marks the promotion as tracking-only: it never draws down real cash, so the gate skips the real-book cash-funding rule (MinCashBuffer) for it while still enforcing concentration/sizing rules (MaxPositionWeight, MaxNewPosition, Turnover). Real (non-paper) promotions keep today's full rule set unchanged.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Application.Commands.ProposeRecommendationCommand
member.summary: Ledger proposes one action on one ticker (#1069). The proposal must be anchored to a trigger that is true right now - a broken thesis, an IPS sleeve outside its band, a position over the single-position cap, a recent Radar signal, or a fired event - and Hold is only an answer to a fired event. The handler sizes it from the book and a quote (Add runs the risk gate and is clamped to the compliant size), writes the exact order text the owner would place at the broker, and queues it silently. Nothing here or downstream sends an order anywhere.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Application.Commands.ProposeThesisRevisionCommand
member.summary: Puts one change to a thesis (or one promotion) to the owner as a pending artifact. Nothing is written to the thesis, the candidate or the book: the owner's confirm is the single step that does that (). A newer proposal on the same subject supersedes the open one. Content is validated now against the same rules a direct save applies, so a proposal the owner could never confirm is refused at the door rather than failing on confirm.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Application.Commands.RunPolicyReviewCommandHandler
member.summary: Opens the scheduled policy review when the statement's recorded cadence says it is due (#696): measures current positioning against the statement's bands, proposes adjustments with their rationale, records the review (which stamps the statement's last-reviewed timestamp) and presents the proposal through the alert → companion path. A review opened past the grace period also reports the missed one. An empty or stale book defers the review, unrecorded, to the next run. Recommend-only: nothing here places, stages or routes an order.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Application.Commands.RunRecommendationTriggersCommand
member.summary: The rule sweep (#1069): for every user with a risk rule set or a thesis, a held name whose thesis broke gets an Exit proposal, and a held name over the single-position cap (not silenced by an acknowledgement) gets a Trim back to the cap. It never replaces a pending proposal, and it does not re-propose a trigger it already put (since the thesis broke, or in the last 30 days for the cap). Proposals are queued silently - nothing is pushed. Runs with no person in scope, so every read is job-safe.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Application.Commands.RunThesisMonitorCommandHandler
member.summary: Evaluates every trigger of every thesis owned by a user and marks unbroken theses broken on the first breaching trigger (OR semantics). Also auto-clears a broken thesis when a fresh evaluation holds for every evaluable trigger (US3) — but never on an all-non-evaluable result, since missing data must not un-break a thesis (FR-013). Every trigger it cannot evaluate is reported in with its reason and the data coverage behind it (#837), so a blind thesis is never reported as quietly intact.

Evaluates every trigger of every thesis owned by a user and marks unbroken theses broken on the first breaching trigger (OR semantics). Also auto-clears a broken thesis when a fresh evaluation holds for every evaluable trigger (US3) — but never on an all-non-evaluable result, since missing data must not un-break a thesis (FR-013). Every trigger it cannot evaluate is reported in with its reason and the data coverage behind it (#837), so a blind thesis is never reported as quietly intact.

The coverage-degradation diff (#1375): the triggers that produced a verdict on the previous run and cannot now, read from the snapshot the previous run stored on the thesis. Raises one alert per thesis naming them, then stores this run's snapshot. A trigger that was already blind last run is not reported again (the post-run blind-spot notice owns that), and a thesis with no snapshot yet (its first monitored run) has nothing to diff. Neither the alert nor the snapshot write may abort the run.

member.summary: A save that omits capacity or drawdown tolerance keeps the recorded values (an amendment for another reason must not silently drop an enforced threshold). It stamps a fresh measurement when it is the first statement, says so explicitly, or changed tolerance, capacity or drawdown tolerance; otherwise the prior measurement carries forward untouched, so a version written for another reason never passes for a re-measurement.

FR-001/FR-002: one Created event per thesis, never on update; a Revised event for a content change. When Ledger made the change the append is part of the write's transaction and a failure rolls the thesis back, so the caller retries a clean write (the audit trail is what makes a Ledger change visible and reversible). The owner's own save keeps the journal best-effort: the append runs after the thesis is committed, and failing the call then would make the caller retry and write another row, since a create carries a fresh id (issue #626). Logged at error, because a lost event has no backfill path (unlike a missing quote, which marks PricesPending for the weekly job).

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Application.Commands.ScoreRecommendationOutcomesCommand
member.summary: Scores decided proposals (#1069). A confirmed Add, Trim or Exit is Executed when an ingested fill on the ticker in the right direction (a buy for Add, a sell for Trim/Exit) lands from a day before the decision (a broker fill is often stamped at midnight, or placed before the owner confirms here) to after it, and Unexecuted once the window closes without one - Finance Sentry only observes the owner's own trades. Confirmed and rejected proposals alike are scored against the S&P 500 from the decision's journal price stamp to today's quote, refreshed daily until have passed. Runs with no person in scope.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Application.Services.BenchmarkTrackRecordMaterializer
member.summary: Materializes the benchmark-relative track record (fs-699) from the persisted paired series — no quotes are fetched here, only stored prices are read. Every thesis with a series counts, closed or deleted ones included, so the record carries no survivorship bias. Each thesis is placed in the asset-class sleeve of its held position (or ), and its net-of-friction figure is released only when the #688 reconciliation marks that brokerage position's cost basis Verified. Book and sleeve rows in sustained underperformance raise an alert; rows that recover resolve it.

member.summary: The research memo on coverage entrants (discovery funnel stage 6), the funnel's only model call. For each ranked coverage add that has no memo yet it makes one single-turn call over evidence the pipeline already stored and keeps the reply as a . Three limits keep the spend bounded and are checked before every call: the mode ( makes no call), across everyone, and a rolling seven-day budget () that the call's worst-case cost must fit under on top of what was already recorded. Entrants a limit passed over stay eligible for . Logged only: nothing reads a memo to act.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Application.Services.Etf.EtfLookThroughReader
member.summary: Looks an ETF through to its top 10 holdings (issue #1324): reads the holdings (), scores each with the same single-name rules a stock gets, and totals the weight reading BUY or better. Holdings are scored one after another because the structure and fundamentals reads share the request's one scoped DbContext. A holding is scored without a look-through of its own, so a fund of funds can never recurse. A holding that cannot be scored counts against the fund and the basis says so; a fund with no holdings at all says that instead.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Application.Services.Fundamentals.FundamentalsChainService
member.summary: The ordered fundamentals provider chain (#837). Sources are asked in Fundamentals:SourceOrder order, and each period basis (quarterly, annual) is supplied whole by ONE source: the first whose series on that basis is fresh. A series is therefore never stitched from two providers, so a margin never divides one provider's operating income by another's revenue. When no source has a fresh series, the freshest stale one is used and flagged. A source that fails (an outage, not "no data") stops the fall-through: a later provider's numbers never stand in for an unreachable earlier one, which would make a deterministic monitor read a different series on a bad night. A ticker the first source covers fully never reaches the others.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Application.Services.MacroCalendarSchedule
member.summary: The authoritative macro release schedule the calendar is reconciled against (#1091), read from each publisher's own calendar: BLS release schedules for CPI and the Employment Situation (08:30 ET), the Fed's FOMC meeting calendar (statement at 14:00 ET on the second day of the meeting) and the ECB's monetary policy calendar (decision at 14:15 Frankfurt time). member.name: F:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Application.Services.NewsSourceHealthTracker.DisableThreshold

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Application.Services.PaperPickHorizon
member.summary: Paper picks (#986): every opportunity candidate, in any status, is a pick graded against the S&P 500 from its price-stamped Created event to a price stamped at the same horizon a decided proposal is scored over (). A promoted, rejected or expired pick is still graded, so a rejection reads as the counterfactual. The horizon point is the first Expired or Snapshot event at or after the horizon and inside of it; a pick whose horizon passed without one is left ungraded rather than priced at a later date.

member.summary:
Turns a deterministic hit on a ticker (a filing, a passed date, a news cluster) into the "take a fresh look" notice for every thesis and Active candidate that name belongs to (the proactive thesis-maintenance loop, step 1). Pure mapping and a single alert call per subject: whether anything actually changed is Ledger's call, never this class's, and no model is consulted. Once-only is the alert generator's job ( keys on subject, source and reference).
A hit on a covered name (a job that opted in through ) is also noted on the subjects, even when the name maps to no thesis or candidate, and hands the noted hits to the coverage event review once the user's pass is over.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Application.Services.ScanShortlistService
member.summary:
Stage 1 of the opportunity funnel (#558): composes the bounded shortlist stage 2 pays per-ticker bar math for, out of three market-wide signals that need no bars at all — the index constituent list, the quote read for the day's percent change, and the street's recent favourable actions — with the EDGAR fundamentals grade applied last, to a slate the cheap signals already bounded.
Cost: the quote read covers the whole index, and IMarketDataService resolves it a ticker at a time behind its cache, so a run costs one light quote fetch per constituent. That is the cheapest market-wide momentum signal available today, but it is not a single batched call — a genuinely batched quote endpoint would cut the request count by an order of magnitude.
Every upstream here degrades rather than throws: no quotes and no actions yields an empty shortlist, which leaves the consuming universe at its core (held + watchlist + lenses) members exactly as it stood before the funnel existed.

member.summary: Reads one symbol's scorecard and its verdict at request time (spec 726 US2): the unchanged 019 scorers via , the 021 regime adjustment, the caller's valuation facts, then . Shared corpus: nothing per-user, nothing persisted, no candidate, signal or alert side effects (those stay with candidate scoring). member.summary: Runs the discovery-funnel screens (stage 5) and feeds what they find into the existing candidate path: a hit becomes a Scan candidate scored by the same the opportunity scan uses, its first nomination reason the screen's tag (what the Ledger scoreboard reads to attribute a coverage add to the screen). The coverage evaluator (stage 1) then decides, with its unchanged rules, whether the candidate earns a place in the user's list. Nothing here adds to coverage, alerts or calls a model.
member.remarks: Per user, a hit is skipped when the name is already covered, when the user already has an Active candidate carrying the screen's tag (so a re-run changes nothing), or when the user's coverage removed it and the evidence is not newer than the removal (). Nominations are capped per screen and per user per run, and by the room left under Coverage:MaxMembers: with none left, the user's candidates would only wait.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Application.Services.ValuationHistoryService
member.summary: Builds a trailing-P/E average from reported diluted-EPS quarters (the fundamentals chain) × Yahoo daily closes (feature 030, R3). At each quarter-end we roll the trailing four quarters into a TTM EPS and price it against the close on/just before that date; the average of those points is the "5-year" trailing P/E, over whatever window the filings actually cover. Deterministic and source-grounded — no fabrication.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Domain.BenchmarkRelativeRecord
member.summary: One materialized benchmark-relative track-record figure (fs-699): the return of a scope (book, sleeve or thesis) against the benchmark over one window, computed by the weekly track-record job from the persisted paired series and stored so the API and the agent read the figure rather than recomputing it. Rows are append-per-run: one run () writes one row per (scope, scope key, window), and a rerun on the same day replaces that run. Returns are percentages (5.0 = 5%). Uncovered windows keep the row with null returns so the gap is visible rather than silently missing.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Domain.Catalyst.CatalystEvent
member.summary: One dated 8-K catalyst (a filing carrying an item the catalyst scan watches) on a reference-universe name and what the pipeline did about it: the discovery-funnel "catalyst detection beyond the ticker feed" stage. The row is the once-only identity of the filing for the user (ticker and accession number, which EDGAR never reuses), so a daily re-read of the same filing is a no-op and never nominates twice. The filing facts are public; the disposition is the user's pipeline's. No model is consulted anywhere on this path.

member.summary: One deterministic hit (a filing, an earnings date, a news cluster) on a covered name and what the pipeline did about it: the discovery-funnel "events on coverage names" stage. member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Domain.Coverage.CoverageMemo
member.summary: The research memo written once for a coverage entrant (discovery funnel stage 6, the funnel's only model call): what the business is, why now, what would make the call wrong, crowding, correlation to the book and a verdict. One row per coverage add (), so a name is never paid for twice for the same entry. Logged only: nothing reads a memo to place, size or change a position or to move a name in or out of coverage; the paper-pick scoreboard grades the entrants before anyone sizes on them. The row records what the call consumed so the weekly spend cap is enforced from stored facts.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Domain.Coverage.CoverageRules
member.summary: The coverage add and remove rules (discovery funnel stage 1): pure and deterministic, no read, no model call. Held and watchlisted names are pinned: always members, never removed. The rest earn a place by a verdict history (Buy or StrongBuy on two days inside the window) or a Ledger nomination with a decision note, and lose it by two consecutive Avoid verdicts, an expired candidate, or NoEventDays without an event and no dated catalyst ahead. A name carrying an active thesis is protected from removal like a held one: its thesis needs it covered.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Domain.Fundamentals.ReturnOnInvestedCapitalPeriod
member.summary: One fiscal year's return on invested capital (#1376): NOPAT / year-end invested capital, where NOPAT = operating income x (1 - effective tax rate), the rate being income tax / pre-tax income (bounded to 0-100%), and invested capital = debt + parent stockholders' equity - cash and cash equivalents (marketable securities are not netted, operating leases are not added). Every input is shown so the figure can be checked; the whole row is null with (naming what is missing or why it cannot be formed) rather than filled with zeros. is borrowings as the filer tags them: the total when it reports one, otherwise the long-term line plus its current borrowings (the current-debt total, else the current portion of long-term debt plus short-term borrowings). When no current borrowings are reported the figure is still computed from the long-term line alone and carries that as a caveat beside the value.

Every input is shown so the figure can be checked; the whole row is null with (naming what is missing or why it cannot be formed) rather than filled with zeros. is borrowings as the filer tags them: the total when it reports one, otherwise the long-term line plus its current borrowings (the current-debt total, else the current portion of long-term debt plus short-term borrowings). When no current borrowings are reported the figure is still computed from the long-term line alone and carries that as a caveat beside the value.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Domain.InvestmentPolicyStatement
member.summary: The user's Investment Policy Statement — the written, versioned strategy that every proactive alert and rebalancing prompt is measured against. Structure follows the CFA Institute / Bogleheads IPS schema: purpose, horizon, risk, target allocation with rebalancing bands, contributions, sell discipline, and constraints. Amended over time: saving a new version supersedes the prior one (IsCurrent flips), keeping history rather than overwriting.

member.name: P:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Domain.InvestmentPolicyStatement.RiskMeasuredAt
member.summary: When tolerance, capacity and drawdown tolerance were last measured with the user (#700). Set by a re-measurement or by a save that changed any of the three; carried forward unchanged by a save that did not touch them, so a version written for another reason never passes for a fresh measurement. Null = never measured (every statement authored before #700).

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Domain.MacroEventTiming
member.summary: When a macro event happens, whether it already has, and the key that names it across date corrections (#1091). A row's / are the publisher's own wall clock (BLS and the Fed publish in US Eastern time, the ECB in Frankfurt time), so the instant is resolved in that zone, never in the server's or the reader's. An untimed row counts from the start of its local day, so it is never announced as still to come on the day itself.

member.name: M:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Domain.MacroEventTiming.ZoneFor(System.String)
member.summary: The zone a region's publishers date their releases in; UTC for a region this calendar does not know.

member.summary: The UTC instant the event is released.

member.name: M:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Domain.MacroEventTiming.StatusAt(System.DateTimeOffset,System.DateTimeOffset)
member.summary: once the release instant is reached, otherwise scheduled.

member.name: M:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Domain.MacroEventTiming.Key(System.String,System.DateOnly)
member.summary: The stable key of one release, macro:{FAMILY}:{yyyy-MM} (e.g. macro:CPI:2026-10 for the September CPI released in October 2026). It names the release, not the row: a date corrected within the month keeps the key, which is what lets the sync recognise a misdated row and lets an announcement fire once per release.

member.name: M:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Domain.MacroEventTiming.Family(System.String)

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Domain.PolicyReviews.PolicyReviewSchedule
member.summary: When the next policy review is due (#696), derived from the statement alone: the cadence comes from the current version, and the anchor is the most recent review recorded on any version — a new version of the statement does not restart the clock. A statement never reviewed is anchored on its first authoring, so its first review falls one cadence after it was written.

member.summary: How late a due review may open before it counts as missed. The review job runs daily, so a review due mid-day opens at the next run; beyond two days at least one scheduled run failed to open it and the lapse itself is reported.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Domain.Positions.PositionReturns
member.summary: Where a holding's return came from, in USD (money-semantics §1, "Return decomposition"): is the open position's price gain at today's FX rate, the average-cost gain locked in by sells, the dividend income net of tax withheld, and what the move in the trade currency's USD rate added to the open cost since the buys. A component is null when the ingested ledger cannot support it; sums the non-null ones. : complete = the fills explain the whole holding; partial = they do not (history before the first ingested fill), so the unrealized figure is the holding's own cost-basis gain and the realized and currency components are null (dividends too when no income row was ingested); unavailable = no fills or dividends were ingested for the symbol. is the open average cost per unit in , set only for complete coverage in a single trade currency.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Domain.PriceRounding
T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Domain.Recommendations.Recommendation
member.summary: One proposal Ledger puts to the owner on one ticker (#1069): an action, the evidence behind it and the exact order it implies. The owner confirms or rejects it; Finance Sentry never places, stages or transmits the order - a confirm records the decision and shows the order text for the owner to place at the broker themselves. At most one row exists per (UserId, Ticker); a newer proposal supersedes it. Rows are never deleted, so every proposal ends in the decision journal as confirmed, rejected, expired or superseded.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Domain.Recommendations.RecommendationSizing
member.summary: Pure sizing for a proposal (#1069). Exit sells the whole position; Trim sells the requested amount or, with none, what takes the position back to the single-position cap; Add buys the requested amount. Whole shares for listed names - a trim rounds up so it reaches the cap, an add rounds down so it stays within it - and six decimals for a fractional (crypto) holding. Cash stays in the book either way, so the book total is the denominator before and after.

member.summary: One change to a thesis (or one promotion) put to the owner as a pending artifact. Ledger proposes through its service token; only the owner's confirm writes the thesis, and it does so through the same commands the owner's own edits use, so a promotion still runs the risk gate. A confirm is therefore the single step that writes. At most one row exists per (UserId, SubjectId); a newer proposal supersedes it. Rows are never deleted: every proposal ends confirmed, rejected, expired or superseded, with the reason kept.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Domain.Scoring.CashFlowMath
member.summary: Cash-flow handling for get_fundamentals (#1376). XBRL cash-flow facts are durations measured from the fiscal-year start (a Q2 10-Q reports six months, a Q3 nine, the 10-K twelve), so a quarter is not a reported fact: it is the year-to-date figure less the previous year-to-date figure of the same year (Q4 = the full year less nine months). Pure and deterministic; a quarter whose subtrahend is missing is left out, never zero-filled.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Domain.Scoring.EtfVerdictRules
member.summary: The small published ETF table (issue #1324): a fund is read by looking through to its top 10 holdings, each scored by the single-name rules, and the fund gets its word from this ordered list, first match fires, like . AVOID on the fund's own structure below the equity AVOID line; BUY needs the fund's structure at the equity BUY bar, crowding not Extended, and more than half of the top-10 weight reading BUY or better. There is no STRONG BUY rule: an ETF word is capped at BUY in v1. A fund whose holdings could not be read can still be AVOID (its own structure), but cannot reach BUY: a missing look-through can only lower the word.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Domain.Scoring.RegimeScoreAdjuster
member.summary:
Pure, deterministic regime→structure-score adjustment (feature 021, US3). Regime is context only: this haircuts the presented/ranked structure score of speculative candidates in risk-off macro conditions, so a chase-machine can't rank a frothy momentum name top-of-list in a crisis. It NEVER actions (no cash-raising, selling, or promotion block — FR-021), NEVER mutates the raw score (which stays governed by FormulaVersion), and is fully explained + reversible (set the config haircuts to 0 to disable).
Rules (magnitudes from ): a volatility haircut in Stressed/Panic scaled by crowding (Extended most penalized, Normal half, Early none), plus an additional inversion haircut when the rates axis is Inverted. Result clamped to [0,100]. When no regime reading is available, the adjusted score equals the raw score with a no_regime_data rationale (FR-022).

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Domain.Scoring.RegimeAdjustment
member.summary: Outcome of the regime adjustment: raw + adjusted structure score, signed delta, rationale, and context.
Outcome of the regime adjustment: raw + adjusted structure score, signed delta, rationale, and context.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Domain.Scoring.ScanNominationRules
member.summary: Pure, deterministic FR-008 nomination rules over the active universe (019 US2): (a) top-quartile RS members of top-N rotating sectors, (b) top-decile RS overall, (c) at the 63-day high on above-average volume. ETF lenses and stale snapshots are never nominated. Reason strings are stable so re-nominations dedup instead of accumulating near-duplicates on the candidate.

member.name: F:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Domain.Scoring.ScanNominationRules.RsWindowBars
member.summary: Window (bars) whose relative strength drives rules (a) and (b).

Re-ranks momentum nominations by a combined quality x momentum score (019 FR-006): the EDGAR fundamentals grade weighted against the universe RS percentile. A nomination missing either half — EDGAR cannot grade crypto/ETFs/non-filers, and a breakout can nominate a ticker with no RS at all — scores no combined value and ranks below every fully-scored name on its RS alone, rather than being dropped or having the missing half defaulted to a faked number. The same rule governs the reason tag: only a name that actually scored on both halves is labelled a quality x momentum pick.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Domain.Scoring.ScanShortlistRules
member.summary:
Stage 1 of the opportunity funnel (#558): pure, deterministic composition of a bounded shortlist out of the index constituent list, using only signals that cost no per-ticker bar math.
The stage is itself cheapest-first. ranks the whole index on two free-or-batched signals — the day's percent change (coarse momentum) and the street's recent favourable actions — and hands back only as many names as a run may afford to grade. then re-ranks that slate on the EDGAR fundamentals grade and caps it at the shortlist size. A name EDGAR cannot grade keeps its surface standing and sorts below every graded name rather than having its missing half defaulted to a faked number (the rule already follows in stage 2).

The index ranked on surface signals alone, truncated to the run's EDGAR grading budget. Only names carrying at least one signal are ranked — a constituent with neither a quote nor a street action is invisible to stage 1 this run rather than filling a slate slot at score zero.
The graded slate re-ranked on quality x surface momentum and capped at — the names stage 2 pays bar math for.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Domain.Scoring.VerdictRules
member.summary: The verdict decision list (spec 726 OQ-4): an ordered list of rules, each a conjunction of axis conditions, where the first rule that matches fires. Pure and deterministic: the same inputs and the same always give the same word (FR-005). Every rule is evaluated and returned so the drill-down shows the whole table, not only the winner (FR-006). There are no points and no weights: a word is never derived from a sum of axes (019 FR-007 as amended). Rules v2 keeps the five words and the table's shape: STRONG BUY also needs revenue growth, the price lens falls back to the forward P/E against peers when the own-history premium is missing, and every WAIT names its reason ().
member.remarks: Null axes are explicit (FR-008): tests for them, and a comparison against a missing axis is never met, so a missing axis can only lower a word. A missing fundamentals axis caps a name at BUY; a missing crowding or valuation axis keeps it from STRONG BUY.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Domain.Valuation.DcfMath
member.summary: Pure discounted-cash-flow math for get_dcf_valuation (#1269). Five-year (3-10) unlevered free-cash-flow projection, mid-year discounting (periods 0.5, 1.5, ...), a Gordon-growth terminal value on the year after the last projected year (discounted over the last cash flow's period) that refuses when g >= WACC, an exit-multiple terminal value for the cross-check, and a bisection solve for the growth rate a price implies. Every grid cell and every solve step is a full recompute through - never a linear approximation - so the centre cell of a grid is the headline by construction. Deterministic; amounts stay in whatever unit the caller supplies (the reporting currency), and nothing here reaches a network or the clock.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Infrastructure.Caching.TtlCache`1
member.summary: A bounded per-key result cache for the provider adapters. Each instance owns a size-limited (the shared has no limit and its entries carry no size), so a long-running process cannot grow it past maxEntries. Freshness is judged on the injected , so tests move time instead of sleeping; the cache's own expiry only evicts. Concurrent misses on one key share a single in-flight fetch (other keys fetch in parallel); the fetch is not tied to any one caller's token, each caller only stops waiting on its own.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Infrastructure.Jobs.AnalystRatingChangeAlertJob
member.summary: Daily Hangfire job (pick 6 of #825, notifications A): turns the street's upgrades and downgrades () into at most one alert per ticker per action day, summarising every firm that moved that day. Covers a user's held equities always, and their watchlist only when the profile's WatchlistAnalystAlerts toggle is on (). Runs after the 01:00 UTC ingestion and looks back days rather than only at today, so an action dated the previous US session (ingested overnight) or a run lost to a deploy still alerts; the generator dedups once per (ticker, day), which makes the overlap a no-op. A name that is both held and watched alerts once. Initiations, target changes and reiterations are not rating changes and never alert.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Infrastructure.Jobs.EarningsAheadJob
member.summary:
Daily Hangfire job (T3, ledger-heartbeat design): raises an EarningsAhead alert for a book, watchlist or thesis ticker () with earnings landing within days, or an ex-dividend date in the same window. Thesis tickers are in scope because a thesis is the strongest statement that a name's report matters (#698: a thesis name reporting in the window was never looked up while it sat outside the book). Yahoo quoteSummary is an external dependency with no contract — a missing field, a null date, or a failed fetch already come back as an empty result from , so a provider hiccup here means no alert this run, never a job failure. dedups per (ticker, event type, event date), so re-running the job on the days leading up to the event never re-alerts it — rare, low-noise by design (~0.1 fires/day).
Coverage names () are looked up in the same call. An earnings date inside the window on one is an event for the coverage review (it moves LastEventAt and re-scores the candidate before the report) but raises no EarningsAhead alert unless the name is in the alert universe above, and no review notice: the date is a catalyst, not a reason to reopen a thesis.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Infrastructure.Jobs.EarningsPassedJob
member.summary: Daily Hangfire job: the post-event counterpart of . When a thesis ticker, a trigger proxy or an Active candidate's ticker had an earnings date inside the last days (the same calendar feed and window the earnings-ahead job reads to resolve its alerts), it raises the thesis-review notice (, source earnings, reference = ticker and date) so Ledger re-reads the thesis against the numbers. Digest lane: the notice is held for the pulse. The window is wider than a day so a restarted scheduler or a missed run loses nothing, and the generator's once-only identity makes the overlap a no-op. A crypto asset ticker is left out (no earnings; the bare symbol resolves to an unrelated listed name), and the calendar feed is an external dependency with no contract: a failed fetch is no signal this run, never a job failure. Coverage names are read too (): passed earnings are the event the coverage review acts on.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Infrastructure.Jobs.FilingWatchJob
member.summary:
Hourly Hangfire job (T2, ledger-heartbeat design): raises a FilingLanded alert when a periodic or current report lands on a holding, thesis or thesis-proxy ticker () — 10-K, 10-Q and 8-K for domestic issuers, and 6-K, 20-F and 40-F for foreign private issuers, which never file the domestic forms (#698: without them a foreign-listed holding could never alert). EDGAR's submissions feed has no push mechanism, so this rereads it every hour and relies on 's dedup — once per (ticker, accession number), which EDGAR never reuses — to make a re-read a no-op for filings already seen. A filing is considered for days after its filing date rather than only on the day itself: every deploy restarts the scheduler, and a same-day-only window silently lost any filing whose day happened to miss the remaining hourly runs. The window is still short enough that a stale or backfilled submissions response cannot surface an old filing. EDGAR is an external dependency with no contract — a missing field, an empty submissions list or a failed fetch already come back as an empty result from (which keeps the submissions cache shorter than the hourly cadence and never caches a failed fetch), so a provider hiccup here means no alert this run, never a job failure. Rare by design (~0.2 fires/day in earnings weeks).
The same filing also raises the thesis-review notice (, source filing, reference = the accession number) for every thesis the ticker is the ticker or a trigger proxy of, and for an Active candidate on it. Candidate tickers outside the detector's universe are read too, for the notice alone: a candidate is not a holding, so it earns no FilingLanded alert of its own.
Coverage names (, held ones first) are read the same way, for the notice and the coverage event review alone (): a filing on a name we only cover moves its LastEventAt, re-scores its candidate and runs the coverage remove rules, with no FilingLanded alert.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Infrastructure.Jobs.GeopoliticsSourceSeedJob
member.summary: Daily Hangfire job (N2, ledger-heartbeat design): registers a Google News RSS query source per thesis for the geopolitics/policy terms its ThesisText mentions (sanctions, tariffs, export controls, rulings, regulation, ...). Q3 option A settles how — this goes through the existing (register_thesis_source) with Kind = "Rss", adding no new . GDELT is the named fallback and is deliberately not built here. A thesis whose text mentions none of the configured terms is skipped, keeping volume low (~0.2 fires/day) — the term match, not every thesis, is the source of a registration. Registration only adds a news_sources row; the 30-min ingestion sweep () and the material-cluster detector (, N1) do the rest through the existing RSS pipeline, so a Google News hiccup — a missing field, an empty feed, a slow response, a malformed entry — is already handled the same way any other registered RSS source's failure is: logged, retried, and only alerted through 's own SyncFailure path after the health tracker's consecutive-failure threshold, never a job failure here. Each source's URL carries its thesis id (as a fragment, never sent to Google), so two theses on the same ticker get separate sources instead of overwriting each other's owner. A URL that is already registered is skipped rather than re-registered, so re-running this job daily is a no-op once a thesis's geopolitics source exists — it never re-enables a source the health tracker retired. The one exception is a source retired for thesis staleness: its URL being built again means the thesis matches those terms again, so it is re-registered. Terms match whole words only (optionally pluralised), so "war" never matches "software".

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Infrastructure.Jobs.IntradayMoveSentinelJob
member.summary: Hangfire job (P1, ledger-heartbeat design), every 15 minutes: raises a MarketStructure alert when a held ticker moves ≥5%, a watchlist ticker moves ≥8%, or either moves ≥3σ against its 20-day daily return volatility. Prices come from , the existing 5-minute Yahoo quote cache — no new live-price fetch path. Yahoo's chart endpoint does not report a marketState, so market hours are an explicit NYSE regular-session check (weekday, 09:30–16:00 America/New_York) plus the quote's own being from today's session (which keeps exchange holidays quiet); a held crypto asset (no exchange session) is evaluated on every tick as long as its price is recent. A missing, stale or malformed quote is silently skipped — never an alert, never a job failure — since Yahoo's quote endpoint has no contract. The 20-day volatility check needs (already used elsewhere in Research for historical closes) only when the plain move threshold did not already fire, and each ticker's volatility is fetched at most once per run, shared across users. Today's in-progress bar is excluded from the window so the move being tested never dampens its own z-score. Fewer than 21 prior daily closes (20 returns) makes the z-score not evaluable — the job never fires on a thin sample. Alerts ride the existing with : only its declared 24-hour, per-reference silence window applies — one per-ticker reference derived here, so a name that keeps moving announces itself once a day, not once every 15 minutes, and an unread earlier alert never swallows a later move. Rare by design (~0.1 fires/day, per the design's observed volume).

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Infrastructure.Jobs.LookaheadSilenceMonitorJob
member.summary: Daily Hangfire job (#698): reports a look-ahead detector that has gone without a single alert while its inputs were non-empty. Both detectors ran green for weeks without ever firing, and a green run that never alerts looks exactly like a quiet market — a scheduled job's failure alert cannot catch it. An equity universe produces an earnings or ex-dividend date and a periodic filing at least once per quarterly reporting cycle, so a full cycle of silence means the detector, its provider feed or its filters stopped matching. The report reuses the operational alert path (), is resolved once the detector fires again or its inputs empty out, and is only raised for a detector that has been scheduled for the whole threshold.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Infrastructure.Jobs.MacroEventAlertJob
member.summary: Hourly fire-once detector for high-importance macro releases (#1091). Per active user and release it raises at most one MacroEventAhead alert while the release is still scheduled and due within , and at most one MacroEventReleased alert in the after it is out — both keyed on the release key (macro:CPI:2026-10) and deduped once per reference, ever, so a re-run, a dismiss or the hourly cadence never announces the same release twice, and a released event is never announced as upcoming. The calendar is reconciled with the schedule first, so a misdated row is corrected before anything reads it. The alerts reach the companion like any other, which is how the reader agent learns of a release instead of working it out from dates.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Infrastructure.Jobs.NewsMaterialityJob
member.summary:
Hangfire job (N1, ledger-heartbeat design): raises a NewsCluster alert when a held name or thesis keyword clusters in the news. Runs every 30 minutes, offset after the news ingestion sweep () so a freshly ingested batch — including per-thesis Google News RSS sources seeded by , N2 — is visible to this run. Fires when, within , a ticker's retrievable articles (#693: those with a usable URL — see ) — those tagged with the ticker (per-ticker feeds) plus those tagged with any of its theses (registered sources, which carry thesis tags but no ticker tags) — either (a) come from two or more distinct sources reporting two or more distinct stories (#693: a story reprinted verbatim by a second distributor is not independent corroboration — see ), (b) include a hit from a source registered to one of the ticker's theses, or (c) mention a term from . dedups per (ticker, day) and article-level ContentHash dedup at ingestion already collapses re-fetched items, so a feed re-reading the same articles every 30 minutes never re-fires. Designed as the loudest signal (~0.3-1 fires/day); the retrievable-article and distinct-story gates above are #693's fix for that rate drifting several times over target, mostly overnight when wire syndication reposts the same story under multiple distributor names.
A cluster on a ticker that maps to a thesis (its own ticker or a trigger proxy) or to an Active candidate also raises the thesis-review notice (, source news, reference = ticker and day, evidence = the article ids). Active-candidate tickers outside the held and thesis names are scanned for that notice alone: a candidate is not a holding, so it earns no NewsCluster alert of its own.
Coverage names () are scanned the same way, for the notice and the coverage event review alone (): a cluster on a name we only cover moves its LastEventAt, re-scores its candidate and runs the coverage remove rules, with no NewsCluster alert.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Infrastructure.Jobs.NewsSourceRecoveryJob
member.summary:
Re-probes news sources the health tracker auto-retired and returns the ones that can fetch again to service (spec 047). Without it, retirement is permanent: only walks enabled sources, and nothing else re-enables a row — so a source that failed for six hours stayed dark for six weeks even after the cause was fixed in code (issue #318).
A probe is a real ingestion, not a ping: articles it fetches are tagged and inserted like any other run. A probe that fails is expected and stays quiet — it refreshes the recorded failure reason so a diagnosis starts from today's error, but leaves alone (that counter means "failures while in service") and raises no alert, since the disable alert for this source already fired.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Infrastructure.Jobs.NewsSourceSeedJob
member.summary:
Idempotently seeds the market-wide default news feeds and the TrendForce → DRAM thesis page source (feature 030, T046/FR-007). Runs on a schedule (and startup) so the defaults exist without a data migration; existing sources (matched by URL) are left untouched. The TrendForce source is only seeded once a DRAM thesis exists — it is skipped gracefully otherwise.
It also repairs rows seeded with a URL we have since corrected (issue #318). Idempotency-by-URL alone cannot fix a row whose URL is the thing that is wrong: #326 changed the TrendForce constant but the deployed row kept pointing at the old marketing hub and kept failing, so the repair pass below rewrites it in place and clears the failure state that had retired it.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Infrastructure.Jobs.ThesisSourceRetirementJob
member.summary:
Daily Hangfire job, paired with : retires a seed-registered news source once its URL is no longer the one the seed would build from its thesis today () — the thesis was edited so its matched terms changed or dropped out entirely, so the source keeps polling under a thesis that no longer says what it said. Sources a user registered to a thesis directly (not seed-built Google News URLs carrying that thesis's marker) are never judged against geopolitics terms here.
This covers only the "text no longer matches" half of thesis-source staleness. The other half — the thesis itself was deleted — is handled synchronously by at delete time, not here: the news_sources.ThesisId foreign key is ON DELETE SET NULL, so by the time a nightly sweep could look, a deleted thesis's id would already be gone from the row — there is nothing left to key a "was this thesis deleted" check off of.
Retirement disables the source ( = false) and records / rather than deleting the row, so a source that stops feeding stays visible for someone to find and explain.
Health and thesis-relevance never fight: this job only reads ThesisId and thesis text — it never inspects or the current value to decide anything, so a source that is merely failing stays the health tracker's problem. A source already retired (RetiredReason != null) is skipped so repeated runs never re-touch it, and excludes retired rows, so never re-probes and revives one just because its feed still happens to fetch.

member.name: M:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Infrastructure.Persistence.Repositories.QuoteCacheRepository.UpsertManyAsync(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyCollection{FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Domain.QuoteCacheEntry},System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary:
Refreshes the cached quotes with one INSERT ... ON CONFLICT over the Ticker primary key: the write is atomic, so two overlapping refreshes update the same rows instead of the loser failing on the key, and no read precedes it. A repeated ticker in the batch keeps its last entry.
The statement runs at once and stages nothing in the shared , which is what issue #626 needs: this context is scoped, so it is the *caller's* unit of work, and every caller treats a quote refresh as best-effort and swallows the failure (ThesisEventRecorder.TryGetPricesAsync, the monitor, the snapshot jobs). Rows left staged by a failed write would survive the swallow and make the next unrelated SaveChangesAsync throw — how a quote-cache fault surfaced as save_thesis failing on every call while reads were fine. A cache is best-effort; its failure must not be contagious. A quote already tracked by this context is not refreshed.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Infrastructure.Persistence.ResearchUserDataEraser
member.summary: Erases a person's Research data. Three tables need care beyond the owned-entity sweep: a thesis's news sources point at it with ON DELETE SET NULL, so deleting the thesis first would turn them into market-wide sources; candidate scores carry no foreign key to their candidate, so they would be left behind; and a research document's UserId is nullable (the shared corpus), so it is not IUserOwned - its chunks and embeddings go with it through the cascade.

member.summary: EDGAR full-text search (efts.sec.gov) for 8-K filings: one query per watched item over a date range, paged, every request spaced by the SEC pacer and sent on the declared-User-Agent sec-edgar client. member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Infrastructure.Sources.NewsSourceFetcher
member.summary:
Fetches one registered and maps it to persistable articles: RSS feeds go through , Page sources through the that claims the URL (feature 030, FR-007/FR-008). Articles come back stamped with the source name, its thesis tags and a content hash.
It is shared rather than private to the ingestion job because a source is fetched from two places: the 30-minute ingestion sweep over enabled sources, and the recovery probe that tries retired ones (spec 047). Both must agree on what fetching a source means — a probe that skipped tagging or hashing would revive a source into a different pipeline than the one that retired it.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Infrastructure.Sources.Sp500ConstituentSource
member.summary: The S&P 500 port. A consumer of the reference-universe table (list sp500, refreshed weekly from its upstream), with the embedded seed as the fallback whenever the table is empty, implausibly small or unreadable - so a fresh database, a failed first refresh or a database blip never empties the broad universe. Registered as a singleton; the answer is cached for (the table changes weekly), shorter after a fallback so a recovered table is picked up quickly.

T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Infrastructure.Sources.YahooFundamentalsSource
member.summary: Yahoo Finance's fundamentals timeseries as a chain source (#837): the same key-less provider the valuation snapshot reads, no crumb or cookie needed for this endpoint. It covers what EDGAR's XBRL cannot — the quarterly results a foreign private issuer only furnishes on 6-K (GRAB) — but serves just the last ~5 quarters and ~4 fiscal years, and its line items are Yahoo's own normalization (its operating income can differ from the filed IFRS figure). Hence last in the default order: the chain only reaches it for a period basis no EDGAR taxonomy supplies fresh. Results (and "no data") are cached per ticker for 12 hours; a failure is not cached.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Modules.Research.Migrations.M011_CleanAnalystActionFirms
member.summary: Data repair: the MarketBeat parser concatenated the "Subscribe to MarketBeat All Access…" promo text onto every ingested Firm value. Firm is part of the unique index idx_analyst_actions_dedup (Ticker, Firm, ActionDate, ActionType), so re-ingestion cannot heal the rows — this migration strips the promo suffix in place. Where a cleaned name would collide on the unique index (a clean row already exists, or two polluted rows clean to the same key) the richer/older row wins and the other is deleted first.
